analysis.title: USA: Warsh Does Not Address October FOMC Meeting but Says "World Has Broadly Conformed to Our Expectations" Since Last Meeting
key_insights: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh did not address the October FOMC meeting at the IMF annual meetings. He said "in the intermeeting period, the world has broadly conformed to our expectations" from the September meeting.

Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman said "I don't feel any urgency for taking further action at this point." San Francisco Fed President Daly, speaking after the firmer than expected September CPI report, said she saw no urgent need "to decide with a limited set of information."
GS reads these comments together as a signal that the FOMC will pause in October. GS still expects a second and final hike in December.
Warsh said the US is experiencing "a massive investment surge" tied to the AI buildout. He also noted a "synchronous tightening in monetary policy around the world" recently.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS reads Fed commentary as pointing to no rate change at the October meeting.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds rate, second and final hike
macro_indicators.reading: Second and final hike expected in December
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS keeps its call for one more hike in December, after the hike at the September meeting, and then a stop.
The firmer print did not shift Fed officials toward urgency. Daly cited the limited information available.

risk_factors: A further firm inflation print could pull the next hike forward from December.
Warsh points to a synchronous global tightening in monetary policy and a large AI-related investment surge.

key_data_points.figure: Second and final hike in December
key_data_points.context: GS expects an October pause, then one more hike in December 2026.
key_data_points.anchor: We continue to expect a second and final hike in December.

theme_stances.key_argument: Warsh, Bowman and Daly comments indicate the FOMC will pause in October, and GS still expects a final hike in December.
theme_stances.evidence: the FOMC is set to pause in October
